newsitem.title: UK: Britain may help islanders to leave Montserrat.
newsitem.headline: Britain may help islanders to leave Montserrat.

text.p: Britain may offer people on Montserrat an assisted package to Britain or to other parts of the Caribbean plus a resettlement grant if they decide to quit their island, ravaged in recent weeks by volcanic eruptions.

International Development Minister George Foulkes told Reuters on Thursday the offer was being considered after geological advice that the Soufriere Hills volcano could continue to rumble for up to five more years.
"That means the south of the island will not be usable," he said in a telephone interview.
Twenty-two people are dead or missing following the most serious eruption so far, on June 25, of the volcano in the south of the tiny British colony in the eastern Caribbean.
Hundreds of other people have fled their homes, leaving behind devastated villages.

Foulkes' cabinet minister boss Clare Short said in a statement earlier that Britain was "drawing up a package of options which will be put to the people of Montserrat to enable them to choose the best future for themselves".
Foulkes said the latest advice from the British Geological Survey showed the volcano will remain active, although without a drastic eruption, for between one and five years.

The package of options would quantify what it would be possible to do on the north of the island and "explore the detail of an assisted package and resettlement grant scheme which could include either the United Kingdom or other parts of the Caribbean", he added.
The island's population has dwindled to around 5,800 from about 11,000 when the volcano roared to life in July 1995. Many people have moved to the neighbouring island of Anguilla.
Foulkes said Britain would consider including these exiles in the resettlement scheme since their presence on Anguilla was straining the local economy and infrastructure.

He said the government had not set a figure for the minimum size of the population on Montserrat for the island to remain viable, pointing out that only just over 2,000 people inhabit Britain's Falkland Islands colony in the south Atlantic.
"As long as there is a significant number of people wishing to remain, I am certain that there is a scheme that can be implemented for keeping the north viable," he said.

The south might then be reoccupied when volcanic conditions allowed. Short announced that Britain is to give Montserrat a further 6.95 million pounds ($11.73 million) in aid to help people hurt or made homeless by the volcanic eruption on the island.
"We are taking emergency action to deal with the crisis in all its aspects," she said in a statement.
Short said Britain would provide 6.5 million pounds to help build emergency shelter for islanders, plus 450,000 pounds for emergency repair work on a temporary hospital. ($1=.5926 Pound)
